$comment: The toolchains the playground can compile for, and the devices each one serves. This is the join between three things that otherwise drift: the driver wasm the browser fetches (driverArtifact, driverFile), the flags the device pass needs (triple, devicePassArgs, offloadTargetPrefix), and the simulator's own device registry (devices). A device id is the key everywhere -- simulator/harness/device.go names a Toolchain and an arch for every entry it builds, website/src/lib/compilePipeline.ts looks the toolchain up here from the id the catalog reported, and website/scripts/prepare-assets.mjs stages one driver and one archive per entry. simulator/harness/device_test.go asserts that every registry entry resolves to a row here, so a device can name a toolchain this file does not have without any of them failing silently. defaultArch is what the shell build path emits when a caller names no device and no arch, and it is per toolchain rather than global: an nvptx row would carry an sm_ target and no gfx name at all. arch is spelled per device because one toolchain covers a whole family: a second AMD part, or an NVIDIA one under a toolchain of its own, is a devices entry and not a new toolchain unless its DRIVER wasm differs. id is the stable key every side looks a row up by, so it must stay put across a label rewording. cdna3generic is listed because it is selectable: its kernels run correctly on gfx942, checked element by element against a CPU reference by website/tests/correctness.test.mjs, which runs every fixture on every device the simulator registry marks selectable. That pass rate is what a regression here would show up as. It is a correctness result over those kernels, not an opcode-coverage or timing-model audit of CDNA3.  gfx942 is what that row maps cdna3generic to; the name MGPUSim's own builder switches on is a different string, carried on the entry as Device.SimulatorType.
